rounds.text: The market is currently mispricing Raja Bahadur International Ltd by focusing on historical stagnation rather than the massive inflection point occurring in its capital structure. While the company struggled with a -21% compounded sales growth over five years [E15], the recent 247% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months signals a dramatic operational turnaround [E21]. This momentum is supported by a 30% compounded profit growth over the last three years [E20], which significantly outpaces the sector median profit growth of 15.8% [E74]. The most critical evidence of future value is the Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) of Rs 185.08 Cr, which has surged 111.4% year-over-year [E40]. This massive investment phase suggests that the company is actively deploying capital to scale, which explains why profit growth is currently outperforming price growth by a ratio of 20.58 [E56]. Conceded: the current valuation metrics, including a P/E of 102x [E1] and a P/B of 10.47x [E2], are significantly higher than sector benchmarks [E6, E7], and the five-year sales decline remains a drag on the company's long-term track record [E60].

The business is currently undergoing a massive capital expenditure phase, evidenced by Capital Work-in-Progress surging by 111.4% to reach ₹185.08 Cr in March 2026 [E40]. This aggressive growth spend is already translating into an inflection in financial performance, highlighted by a phenomenal 247% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21]. This explosive earnings momentum vastly outpaces the broader sector median profit growth of 15.8% [E74]. Furthermore, short-term trends confirm a strong operational turnaround, marked by a multi-year sales uptrend [E67] alongside a 3-year compounded sales growth of 15% [E16] and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 30% [E20]. Profit growth is now aggressively exceeding one-year price growth by 235%, signalling that the company is only beginning to outperform expectations [E56]. Conceded: trades at a high P/E of 102 [E1] and a price-to-book of 10.47x [E2] with a poor 5-year sales growth of -21.1% [E60].
